Treat the two conjuncts independently.

1. Use the multiplicative–additive equivalence `G ≃+ Additive G`. It sends `H` to `H.toAddSubgroup` and induces an equivalence between the corresponding coset spaces. Hence one quotient is finite exactly when the other is, giving equality/invariance of finite index under `Subgroup.toAddSubgroup`.

2. Let `U = (𝓞 K)ˣ` and `T = NumberField.Units.torsion K`. The key input is that `T` is finite—the torsion units are the finitely many roots of unity in a number field. Since `U` is abelian,
   \[
   s \sqcup T = sT,
   \]
   so every coset of `s` in `s ⊔ T` has a representative in `T`. Thus `s` has finite index in `s ⊔ T`. Now use finite-index transitivity along
   \[
   s \le s \sqcup T \le U.
   \]
   If `s` has finite index, any larger subgroup does; conversely, finite index of `s ⊔ T`, combined with the finite index of `s` inside it, implies finite index of `s` in `U`.

Finally combine these two equivalences with `And.intro`.
